key_insight: AI and machine learning are becoming core enablers in chemical engineering by combining data-driven prediction with first-principles knowledge across scales from atoms to full processes.
engineering_relevance: These methods can improve materials discovery, transport and thermodynamics modeling, separations, process design, and industrial operations while supporting more reliable and sustainable decision-making.
method: Hybrid physics-informed models that embed conservation laws and thermodynamic constraints
Machine learning integrated with first-principles simulations for prediction and discovery
Human-AI workflows that present information at the right abstraction level for engineering decisions
evidence_signal: The paper is a perspective synthesized from recent methodological developments and representative applications rather than a single benchmark study, emphasizing broad cross-domain adoption.
watch_item: A key implementation concern is managing data scarcity, extrapolation risk, interpretability, and model lifecycle maintenance when deploying AI/ML in high-stakes engineering settings.
paper_title: Atoms to Processes: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Chemical Engineering
